defects.description: After today's run, the next run is calculated by adding 24 hours in milliseconds, which can shift the wall-clock time and schedule the same local date twice across a daylight-saving transition.

trigger.input: node --input-type=module -e 'process.env.TZ = "America/New_York"; const { nextRunAt } = await import("./src/schedule.js"); const first = nextRunAt({ now: () => new Date("2024-11-02T07:00:00-04:00") }); const second = nextRunAt({ now: () => new Date(first.getTime() + 15 * 60_000) }); console.log(JSON.stringify([first.toString(), second.toString()]));'
trigger.expected: ["Sun Nov 03 2024 02:30:00 GMT-0500 (Eastern Standard Time)","Mon Nov 04 2024 02:30:00 GMT-0500 (Eastern Standard Time)"]
trigger.actual: ["Sun Nov 03 2024 01:30:00 GMT-0500 (Eastern Standard Time)","Sun Nov 03 2024 02:30:00 GMT-0500 (Eastern Standard Time)"]

defects.why_missed: The happy suite schedules dates within one UTC offset, where adding 24 hours lands on the next local day at the configured time.

traps.description: The optional helper applies an independent random offset of up to five minutes in either direction, as documented.
